channel.title: Rajat Malik — articles and notes
channel.description: Original, practical articles on Angular and React performance, micro-frontend architecture, design systems, accessibility and AI-assisted frontend delivery.

item.title: The Angular performance checklist I run before every release
item.dc:creator: Rajat Malik
item.description: A field-before-lab checklist covering change detection, bundle size, rendering strategy, images, runtime leaks and the regression guards that keep a fast Angular app fast.

item.title: Where micro-frontend boundaries should actually go
item.dc:creator: Rajat Malik
item.description: Most micro-frontend pain is a boundary problem, not a tooling problem. How to split by ownership, define the shell contract, share less and test independent deployability.

item.title: Core Web Vitals in 2026: the order of operations that moves the needle
item.dc:creator: Rajat Malik
item.description: LCP, INP and CLS reward different fixes. A practical sequence for deciding what to work on first, with the field-data checks that stop you optimising the wrong thing.

item.title: Design systems that survive: tokens, contracts and honest review
item.dc:creator: Rajat Malik
item.description: Why component libraries decay, how to design token and component APIs teams can adopt, and the governance and versioning that keep a design system healthy.

item.title: AI-assisted frontend development without lowering the bar
item.dc:creator: Rajat Malik
item.description: Where LLMs genuinely help frontend teams, where they add risk, and the review, testing and security gates that turn a speed-up into durable quality.

item.title: A WCAG 2.2 checklist for component libraries
item.dc:creator: Rajat Malik
item.description: The accessibility checks that belong at component level, what changed in WCAG 2.2, and how to test beyond an automated scan with keyboard and screen readers.
